source.author: K. Robold
source.title: Wärmetransport im Inneren und in der Randzone von Kugelschüttungen
source.download_method: Connected Chrome; new tab; ordinary PDF viewer Download; no access challenge

conditions.method: Effective bed conductivity inferred from transient radial temperature profiles during heating/cooling; wall inferred using gradients under quasistationary heat transport. Printed pp103-108.
conditions.convection: Printed p105 reports natural convection excluded experimentally from isothermal axial profiles at the stated helium pressure.

uncertainty.reported: Printed p108: plotted results are experiment-specific least-squares means; error bars are standard deviations of experimental results around those means, generally separated into low/high temperature ranges.
uncertainty.digitization: Only clearly identified marker centers are digitized, not theory lines. Conservative reading allowance ±10 K and ±0.05 W/(m K); endpoint markers at the right border ±15 K. These are reading allowances, not confidence intervals or original experimental uncertainty.
uncertainty.total_measurement_uncertainty: Not established from cited pages. Do not combine digitization allowance and plotted standard deviations without an uncertainty model.

scope: These 31.6 mm static zirconia-bed data reach roughly 5-5.3 W/(m K) near 1700 K. They do not establish a measured 12 W/(m K) transport property, and do not directly validate a 9.525 mm flowing-air reactor at 2500 K. No extrapolation or simulation performed.

unavailable.raw_tabulated_measurement_data: Not supplied in the inspected results section; PDF contains no embedded file attachments.
unavailable.exact_vacuum_pressure: Not located in cited experimental pages.
unavailable.sphere_composition_or_stabilizer_fractio: Not established in cited pages; solid input source /13/ concerns ZrO2-CaO, which does not by itself establish the bed specimen composition.

page_exports: PNGs are lossless exports of the original full-page embedded scan bitmap, preserving original orientation and resolution. Selected-page PDF is a derived 3-page extraction, not the unchanged source.
